# 1 Clement Chapter 28 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 28 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_028_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 28

**28:1** Since all things are seen and heard by him, then, let us fear him and abandon the foul desires of wicked works, that we may be covered by his mercy from the coming judgments.

**28:2** For to where can any one of us flee from his mighty hand? And what world will receive one who deserts from him? For the scripture says somewhere:

**28:3** "Where shall I go and where shall I be hid from your face? If I ascend into heaven, you are there; if I go to the ends of the earth, there is your right hand; if I make my bed in the abyss, there is your Spirit."

**28:4** Where then can a person depart, or where can he flee, from him who encompasses all things?

---

*LOGOS preserves the formal rhetorical questions and their escalating structure. "Abyss" for *abyssos* (v. 3) is more precise than "depths."*
